entities.name: Leo of Ostia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Leo Marsicanus or Ostiensis, also known as Leone dei Conti di Marsi, was a nobleman and monk of Monte Cassino around 1061 and Italian cardinal from the 12th century.

Born into the noble family of Marsi, Leo was educated at Monte Cassino and later became a monk, dedicating his life to the Benedictine order.

In 1077, Leo was elected as the cardinal of Ostia, becoming the third cardinal of the church.

As a cardinal, Leo played a significant role in the election of Pope Gregory VII, who would go on to reform the Catholic Church and shape the course of European history.

Despite his influential position, Leo's life was not without controversy, as he was accused of simony and other moral transgressions.

Leo died on May 29, 1115, leaving behind a legacy as a key figure in the history of the Catholic Church.

"The Lord has shown us the importance of humility and obedience." - Leo Marsicanus, quoted in the Annals of the World

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Leo's life and legacy are significant in the history of the Catholic Church, as he played a key role in the election of Pope Gregory VII and the reform of the Church. His controversy surrounding simony highlights the complex nature of power and morality in medieval Europe.
